etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French retirer (“draw back”), from Old French retirer, built from re- (“back”) + tirer (“draw, pull”), the latter from Vulgar Latin *tīrāre, of highly uncertain origin.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To stop working on a permanent basis, usually because of old age or illness.

quote.citation: 2022 September 21, Chris Green tells Nick Brodrick, “It's absolutely my favourite train”, in RAIL, number 966, page 37:
quote.text: Green will never forget "that was the day I retired - the absolute crowning event of my life and I was very proud of that.

definitions.definition: (intransitive, sports) To stop playing their sport and in competitions a sports player.
(transitive, sometimes reflexive) To withdraw; to take away.

quote.citation: a. 1587, Philippe Sidnei [i.e., Philip Sidney], “(please specify the folio)”, in [Fulke Greville; Matthew Gwinne; John Florio], editors, The Countesse of Pembrokes Arcadia [The New Arcadia], London:  […]  [John Windet] for William Ponsonbie, published 1590, →OCLC:
quote.text: He  […]  retired himself, his wife, and children into a forest.

quote.citation: 1592, John Davies, The Original, Nature, and Immortality of the Soul:
quote.text: As when the sun is present all the year, / And never doth retire his golden ray.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To cease use or production of something.

quote.citation: 2020 May 20, John Crosse, “Soon to be gone... but never forgotten”, in Rail, page 63:
quote.text: Only now, due to the COVID-19-associated drop in traffic, are they being retired with 12 of the 30 trains moved to Landore (Swansea) for warm storage.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To withdraw from circulation, or from the market; to take up and pay.
(transitive) To cause to retire; specifically, to designate as no longer qualified for active service; to place on the retired list.

quote.citation: 1988 November 27, “How Richard Gere Learned To Reach Out”, in Parade (The Spokesman-Review), page 10, column 3:
quote.text: How had it felt, at 28, to be the hottest young actor in town? He [Richard Gere] grinned. “It was great having the attention,” he said. “I thought: ‘This is it! I’ve done it! I’m going to retire my father. I’m putting money away for college for my sisters,’ the whole thing. It’s incredibly euphorious. All of a sudden the rehearsal period of your life is over, and your future has arrived. It’s liberating.”

quote.citation: 2023 October 19, Brendan I. Koerner, “Watch This Guy Work, and You’ll Finally Understand the TikTok Era”, in Wired‎[1], →ISSN:
quote.text: By the time I first spoke to Magana in late 2022, 25/7 Media’s success had given him some measure of financial security. “The truth is that I just retired my parents,” he told me two days after Christmas.

definitions.definition: (intransitive, cricket, of a batsman) To voluntarily stop batting before being dismissed so that the next batsman can bat.

(transitive, baseball, of a fielder) To make a play which results in a runner or the batter being out, either by means of a put out, fly out or strikeout. Also, when such an event ends a team's turn at bat.
(intransitive) To go back or return; to withdraw or retreat, especially from public view; to go into privacy.
(intransitive) To retreat from action or danger; to withdraw for safety or pleasure.
(intransitive) To recede; to fall or bend back.

quote.citation: 1944 November and December, “"Duplex Roomette" Sleeping Cars”, in Railway Magazine, page 324:
quote.text: In the daytime the beds are made up but completely out of sight, giving the passenger a comfortable little private room; as the time for retiring comes, after preparing for rest in the same spacious conditions, he is able, practically at a touch, to pull the bed into position ready for use.

definitions.definition: (rare) The act of retiring, or the state of being retired.
A place to which one retires.
(dated) A call sounded on a bugle, announcing to skirmishers that they are to retire, or fall back.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From re- +‎ tire.

definitions.definition: (transitive, American spelling) To fit (a vehicle) with new tires.
